sources.author: jjmata
sources.summary: Requests bounded scaling with shared database/Redis capacity budgets, including all web processes, worker replicas, deployment overlap and operator headroom. A single operational request; not market-size evidence.
Reports action alternatives collapsing through provider schema conversion. Provider-wide causal claims are the reporter's account, not reproduced here.

sources.author: MarcinDudekDev
sources.summary: Requests a read-only list of work owned by a session and describes gaps in external process/transcript inference.

comparison.demand: One concrete November9 shared-capacity planning request, plus primary pooling/deployment documentation.
comparison.distinctValue: Interactive replica-combination matrix with explicit holder arithmetic and portable plans. Connection budgeting itself and manifest analysis already exist in ConnBudget.
comparison.demo: Single offline HTML file with a visible synthetic steady-versus-rollout counterexample.
comparison.discoverability: Database pooling, autoscaling and rollout budgeting have a clear operations audience; actual reach and adoption remain unproven.

comparison.distinctValue: Case-based dual-schema checks could explain lost action branches, but LLM JSON Schema, MCP Inspector and schema test/diff tooling overlap strongly.
comparison.demo: Easy local schema/case demo; establishing actual provider behavior requires version-pinned SDK wire captures.
comparison.discoverability: Active MCP ecosystem, crowded tooling and previous portfolio's concentration in agent utilities.

comparison.distinctValue: Explicit ownership evidence could help, but ProcessKit and existing process managers supervise wrapped jobs; unwrapped detached work and harness subagent state remain ambiguous.
comparison.demo: A reliable cross-platform live demo needs ownership instrumentation; an offline process-tree visualization would duplicate prior portfolio work without satisfying the request.
comparison.discoverability: Strong recognizable problem for agent users, with hard platform-specific reliability boundaries.

competitors.name: ConnBudget
competitors.observedCapability: Static connection budgeting, native/Compose/ECS/Kubernetes inputs, scaling/rolling deployment and PgBouncer-aware estimates. Direct conceptual overlap.

competitors.name: Database Connection Pool Calculator
competitors.observedCapability: Interactive holder model, connection budget and surge headroom. A calculator alternative, not verified by benchmark.

competitors.name: LLM JSON Schema
competitors.observedCapability: CLI/library/browser provider transforms and rule explanations; substantial overlap with schema tooling candidate.

competitors.name: ProcessKit
competitors.observedCapability: Registry-backed supervised/detached runs, list/inspect/wait controls; relevant prior art for process inventory candidate.

trendContext.label: Today's rolling snapshot, not a November9 ranking or observed historical daily star gain.

portfolioResponse: All ten existing tracked repositories observed November10 remain at zero stars and forks with no public issues/PRs. No measured traction leader; a broader operations audience is a hypothesis, not a proven better category.
rationale: Choose a complete local planning workflow with inspectable arithmetic and a directly visible boundary. Make no unique-technology, performance-sizing or star-growth claim.
